answer: Sybil resistance rests on staked enrolment: every identity posts a bond in the chain token, locked per identity, not per operator. A thousand clones lock a thousand pledges yet earn no extra payout, so flood cost scales linearly with identity count. Each epoch a beacon from the prior checkpoint hash must be cited in every proof of work, so pre-minted identities age out. Slashing adds a delta: any gap between a claim and evidence burns the stake, while rewards sit below the pledge, making mass deception negative-EV. There is no walnut shortcut; identity is a cost curve the attacker pre-funds.
